statement.sr:
Pored živopisne prirode od koje zastaje dah, na obroncima planine Miroč, u srcu Nacionalnog parka Đerdap, krije se i jedna zanimljiva priča.

Još od davnina održao se običaj okupljanja stoke u zajednički tor. Taj običaj se kod nas naziva bačija.

Junakinja ove priče je baka Mileva, koja se čuvanjem ovaca bavi još od detinjstva. Iako je u poznim godinama, svakodnevno energično prelazi i više od deset kilometara nepristupačnog terena, kroz guste šume i prostrane livade.

Jutro počinje ispijanjem prve kafe, a zatim sledi ručna muža, koju vredne žene zajedničkim snagama obavljaju veoma brzo.

Dok druge žene od mleka kasnije prave sir, Mileva kreće u svoju dnevnu rutinu.

Kada se ispaša završi i ovce budu site, dan se privodi kraju večernjom mužom, nakon koje se Mileva vraća u svoj skromni dom.

Njen posao se ciklično ponavlja sve dok ima zelene trave i dok snežni smetovi ne zaveju pašnjake. Tada se ovce razdvajaju i vraćaju svojim vlasnicima, kod kojih prezimljuju čekajući novo proleće.

Ova serija fotografija nastala je kao završni rad drugog semestra prve godine studija na Odseku za fotografiju Akademije umetnosti u Novom Sadu, pod mentorstvom prof. dr um. Jelene Kovačević Vorgučin.

Seriju čine fotografije dobijene skeniranjem negativa, kao i digitalne fotografije nastale kao nezavisna dopuna radu.
statement.en:
Beyond the breathtakingly vivid natural landscape, on the slopes of Mount Miroč in the heart of Đerdap National Park, lies a remarkable story.

Since time immemorial, people here have kept the custom of gathering livestock in a shared pen. This practice is known locally as a bačija.

The protagonist of this story is Grandma Mileva, who has tended sheep since childhood. Though now in her later years, she energetically walks more than ten kilometres each day across difficult terrain, through dense forests and vast meadows.

The morning begins with a first cup of coffee, followed by hand-milking, which the hardworking women carry out together with remarkable speed.

While the other women later make cheese from the milk, Mileva sets off on her daily routine.

When grazing is over and the sheep have had their fill, the day comes to an end with the evening milking, after which Mileva returns to her modest home.

Her work follows the same cycle for as long as green grass grows and snowdrifts have not yet buried the pastures. Then the sheep are separated and returned to their owners, where they spend the winter waiting for a new spring.

This photographic series was created as my final project for the second semester of my first year in the Photography Department at the Academy of Arts in Novi Sad, under the mentorship of Prof. Jelena Kovačević Vorgučin, PhD.

The series consists of photographs made by scanning negatives, as well as digital photographs created as an independent extension of the work.

statement.sr:
Ovaj rad predstavlja interdisciplinarno istraživanje pozicije umetničkog dela u prostoru savremene umetničke prakse. Fotografisao sam šumske pejzaže koristeći modifikovan HDR proces u samoj aplikaciji, kombinujući više ekspozicija različitog trajanja. Na taj način sam ih izmestio iz stvarnosti u latentni prostor — prostor koji funkcioniše kao mentalna mapa, a ne kao dokumentarni zapis.¹ U tom procesu priroda mi je bila polazna tačka: mesto koje povezujem sa mirom i sigurnošću, a koje sam odlučio da pretvorim u nešto nestabilno i nepoznato, kao vizuelni ekvivalent unutrašnjeg stanja koje nije uvek vidljivo spolja.

Šuma je tako postala digitalno, virtuelno mesto — nestabilno, čudno, mesto koje pomera granicu između poznatog i nepoznatog.

Posle izvesnog vremena odlučio sam da te digitalne fotografije dodatno obradim. Oslanjajući se na svoju fascinaciju unapred treniranim ONNX modelima — koje mogu da pokrenem čak i na telefonu — kolorizovao sam ih.² Taj čin kolorizacije, vraćanja boje nečemu što je bilo lišeno boje, za mene nosi ideju postepenog vraćanja ravnoteži — procesa koji se odvija polako, kroz greške i halucinantnu interpretaciju modela,³ ali ipak ide ka nečemu celovitijem.

To je sada čudan digitalni san koji se otvara ka novoj enigmi.

¹ Latent space — U mašinskom učenju, latentni prostor je kompresovana, apstraktna reprezentacija podataka u kojoj slične stavke zauzimaju bliske tačke; koristi se za generisanje novih primera interpolacijom. Za umetničku upotrebu, vidi: Yee-King, M. (2022). Latent spaces: A creative approach. In The Language of Creative AI (pp. 137–154). Springer. https://scholar.google.com.mx/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=VND7iOIAAAAJ&sortby=pubdate&citation_for_view=VND7iOIAAAAJ:3s1wT3WcHBgC

² ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) — Otvoreni standard za predstavljanje modela mašinskog učenja, razvijen da omogući prenos modela između različitih framework-a i izvršavanje na različitim uređajima. Zvanična specifikacija: Open Neural Network Exchange Intermediate Representation (ONNX IR) Specification. https://onnx.ai/onnx/repo-docs/IR.html ; istorijat i ekosistem: Open Neural Network Exchange, Wikipedia. https://browse.library.kiwix.org/content/wikipedia_en_all_maxi/Open_Neural_Network_Exchange

³ AI hallucination — Fenomen u kome generativni modeli proizvode izlaz koji je naizgled uverljiv, ali činjenično netačan, nedosledan ili besmislen; kod slika, model može da „vidi“ ili generiše elemente koji nisu prisutni. Pregled: Ho, Z. Y., Liang, S., & Tao, D. Understanding Hallucinations in Large Visual and Language Models. ACM Computing Surveys. https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3811409 ; popularniji prikaz: Visual Hallucinations in LLMs, Communications of the ACM. https://cacm.acm.org/news/visual-hallucinations-in-llms/
statement.en:
This work presents an interdisciplinary exploration of the position of the artwork within the space of contemporary artistic practice. I photographed forest landscapes using a modified in-app HDR process, combining multiple exposures of varying durations. In doing so, I displaced them from reality into a latent space — a space that functions as a mental map rather than a documentary record.¹ In this process, nature served as my starting point: a place I associate with peace and safety, which I chose to transform into something unstable and unfamiliar, as a visual equivalent of an internal state that isn't always visible from the outside.

The forest thus became a digital, virtual place — unstable, strange, a place that shifts the boundary between the known and the unknown.

After some time, I decided to process these digital photographs further. Drawing on my fascination with pretrained ONNX models — which I can run even on my phone — I colorized them.² This act of colorization, of returning color to something that had been drained of it, carries for me the idea of a gradual return to balance — a process that unfolds slowly, through errors and the model's hallucinated interpretation,³ yet still moves toward something more whole.

It is now a strange digital dream that opens onto a new enigma.

¹ Latent space — In machine learning, a latent space is a compressed, abstract representation of data in which similar items occupy nearby points; it is used to generate new examples through interpolation. For an artistic application, see: Yee-King, M. (2022). “Latent spaces: A creative approach.” In The Language of Creative AI (pp. 137–154). Springer. https://scholar.google.com.mx/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=VND7iOIAAAAJ&sortby=pubdate&citation_for_view=VND7iOIAAAAJ:3s1wT3WcHBgC

² ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) — An open standard for representing machine-learning models, developed to enable models to be transferred between frameworks and run on different devices. Official specification: Open Neural Network Exchange Intermediate Representation (ONNX IR) Specification. https://onnx.ai/onnx/repo-docs/IR.html ; history and ecosystem: Open Neural Network Exchange, Wikipedia. https://browse.library.kiwix.org/content/wikipedia_en_all_maxi/Open_Neural_Network_Exchange

³ AI hallucination — A phenomenon in which generative models produce output that appears convincing but is factually inaccurate, inconsistent, or nonsensical; in images, a model may “see” or generate elements that are not present. Overview: Ho, Z. Y., Liang, S., & Tao, D. Understanding Hallucinations in Large Visual and Language Models. ACM Computing Surveys. https://dl.acm.org/doi/pdf/10.1145/3811409 ; a more accessible account: Visual Hallucinations in LLMs, Communications of the ACM. https://cacm.acm.org/news/visual-hallucinations-in-llms/

statement.sr:
Rad „Levitacije“ na prvi pogled deluje kao skup međusobno nepovezanih fotografija, koje ne uspostavljaju ni jasnu serijsku ni konceptualnu celinu. Upravo u toj prividnoj nepovezanosti leži suština rada.
U njegovom središtu nalazi se unutrašnji monolog kao neprekidan filozofski proces, bez jasnog početka i konačnog završetka. Kroz ponavljanje i ponovno proživljavanje trenutaka, posredstvom posmatranja digitalnih otisaka, rad istražuje subjektivni doživljaj stvarnosti i beskonačnu potragu za odgovorima na pitanja egzistencije i smisla bivstvovanja.

Oslanjajući se na Sinestetiku i njene teorijske dodire sa Novom fenomenologijom, rad istražuje osećajnu i afektivnu dimenziju iskustva. Fotografije postaju fragmenti unutrašnjeg iskustva, tragovi misli i pokušaji spoznaje sveta. Taj poetski i simbolički proces odvija se kroz svakodnevnu unutrašnju borbu, u susretu sa svetom, njegovim radostima i bolima.

Ljubav, strah, mržnja i smrt ostaju večne sile koje oblikuju i ograničavaju ljudsko postojanje.
statement.en:
At first glance, the work Levitations appears to be a collection of unrelated photographs that form neither a clear series nor a conceptual whole. It is precisely this apparent lack of connection that lies at the heart of the work.

At its centre is an inner monologue: an uninterrupted philosophical process with no clear beginning or final conclusion. Through repetition and the reliving of moments, mediated by the viewing of digital prints, the work explores the subjective experience of reality and the endless search for answers to questions of existence and the meaning of being.

Drawing on Synesthetics and its theoretical points of contact with New Phenomenology, the work explores the sensory and affective dimensions of experience. The photographs become fragments of inner experience, traces of thought, and attempts to comprehend the world. This poetic and symbolic process unfolds through an everyday inner struggle, in encounters with the world and its joys and sorrows.

Love, fear, hatred, and death remain eternal forces that shape and constrain human existence.

statement.sr:
Rad predstavlja fotografije napuštenih domaćinstava na planini Miroč.
Ova domaćinstva napuštena su pre mnogo godina. Njihovi poslednji stanovnici odavno su se odselili ili preminuli. Vreme, kao nezaobilazni činilac propadanja, počelo je da ostavlja svoj neizbrisiv trag i na ovim objektima.
Priroda i njeni žitelji postepeno zauzimaju prostor koji su nekada nastanjivali ljudi, pronalazeći u njemu nova skloništa.

Na kraju, preostaje samo nada da će se neko jednog dana vratiti i ponovo, kao nekada, rasplamsati radost oko davno ugašenih ognjišta.

Rad „Nada“ dobio je pohvalu žirija na studentskom konkursu za arhitektonsku fotografiju – Nagrada „Maja Momirov“, u organizaciji Udruženja BAZA, Novi Sad, 2026.
statement.en:
This work presents photographs of abandoned homesteads on Mount Miroč.

These homes were abandoned many years ago. Their last inhabitants moved away or passed on long ago. Time, an inevitable agent of decay, has begun to leave its indelible mark on these buildings as well. Nature and its inhabitants are gradually reclaiming the spaces people once occupied, finding new shelter there.

In the end, all that remains is the hope that someone will return one day and rekindle joy around the long-extinguished hearths, as in days gone by.

The work Hope received an honourable mention from the jury in the Maja Momirov Award student competition for architectural photography, organised by the BAZA Association in Novi Sad in 2026.

statement.sr:
Nikada nisam voleo da pozujem pred kamerom. Uvek sam bio iza nje…

Odlučio sam da to promenim, bar jednom. Ideja mi je bila da se prikažem u praistorijskom prostoru — prostoru u kojem čovek počinje da stiče znanje, baš kao što ja, prvi put, doživljavam kako je to biti model.

Taj praistorijski prostor je mesto gde čovek stvara svoja prva umetnička dela, mesto gde je siguran i slobodan — pre jezika, pre stida, pre svih uloga koje kasnije prihvatamo. To je mesto potpune ranjivosti, ali i radikalne iskrenosti tela: tela bez maske, bez poze naučene pred kamerom, bez unapred stvorenog identiteta.

Trenutak kada novorođenče izlazi iz majčine utrobe je isti taj trenutak — prvi susret sa svetom, pre nego što telo nauči da se predstavi, pre nego što nauči da se sakrije. Postaviti se pred kameru u toj poziciji znači vratiti se na početak: odbaciti ulogu autora i posmatrača i, prvi put, jednostavno biti telo koje se pojavljuje.
statement.en:
I have never been fond of posing in front of a camera. I was always behind it…

I decided to change that, at least once. My idea was to depict myself within a prehistoric space — a space where man begins to gain knowledge, just as I, for the first time, am learning what it feels like to be a model.

That prehistoric space is where man creates his first works of art, a place where he is safe and free — before language, before shame, before all the roles we later come to assume. It is a place of complete vulnerability, but also of radical honesty of the body: a body without a mask, without a pose learned in front of a camera, without a preconceived identity.

The moment a newborn emerges from its mother's womb is the same moment — the first encounter with the world, before the body learns to present itself, before it learns to hide. To place myself in front of the camera in that position means returning to the beginning: shedding the role of author and observer, and, for the first time, simply being a body that appears.

statement.sr:
Rođen sam u prirodi i odrastao okružen njome, mnogo pre nego što sam upoznao bilo šta izvan nje. Detinjstvo sam proveo u kući bez struje. Doslovno. Bez računara, bez telefona, a televiziju sam gledao samo povremeno, poput nekog pozajmljenog sna. Možda je upravo zato nekima teško da poveruju da sam se kasnije vratio da ponovo živim u porodičnoj kući.

Priroda je oduvek bila moje neposredno okruženje. Doživljavam je kao preobilje zelenila, zasićeno živim, neukroćenim bojama. Cveće je svuda — neuređeno, živo, neobuzdano. U njemu se krije čitav sistem oblika, struktura i obrazaca. Ako dovoljno pažljivo posmatraš, počinje da liči na neki drugi jezik. Livada je moj univerzum. Gotovo sve čega se sećam iz detinjstva vezano je za nju: cveće, trava, suncem užarena popodneva... i još cveća.

Cveće? Koji đavo? Zašto je onda sve crno-belo? I dalje?

Za ovu seriju koristim prethodno obučen model neuronske mreže za transformaciju slike u sliku (image-to-image), koji se izvršava lokalno putem ONNX Runtime okruženja. Model radi isključivo sa crno-belim slikama, obrađujući informacije o svetlini i strukturi, i transformišući fotografski materijal kroz sopstvenu interpretaciju oblika, teksture i kontrasta. Dobijene slike nisu ni neposredni fotografski zapisi ni potpuno zamišljene konstrukcije. One nastaju negde između izvorne fotografije i unutrašnjih reprezentacija modela.

Zanima me upravo taj prostor transformacije, u kojem fotografska slika postaje nešto rekonstruisano, a ne samo zabeleženo — proces u kojem se prepliću percepcija, sećanje i mašinska obrada.
Povremeno se vraćam u ovo ruralnom okruženje sa ograničenom infrastrukturom, gde se moj telefon i digitalni alati napajaju solarnom energijom. Ovde tehnologija nije apstraktna niti udaljena. Ona predstavlja praktičan i opipljiv sistem, oblikovan sopstvenim ograničenjima i uslovima u kojima funkcioniše. Dok priroda biva moje neposredno okruženje, tehnologija postaje sredstvo pomoću kojeg je posmatram na drugačiji način.

Rad sa laganim AI modelima koji se izvršavaju lokalno omogućava mi da proširim sopstvenu fotografsku praksu izvan okvira konvencionalne digitalne obrade slike. Umesto pukog menjanja fotografije, istražujem transformaciju, rekonstrukciju i mogućnosti posmatranja poznatog okruženja kroz specifičan vizuelni jezik.

Na kraju, ovaj rad odražava moj odnos prema dva naizgled udaljena sveta: prirodnom okruženju u kojem sam odrastao i tehnološkim sistemima kroz koje ga danas ponovo interpretiram. Tehnologiju ne posmatram kao zamenu za prirodu ili ljudsku percepciju, već kao još jedno sredstvo za proširivanje granica njihovog doživljaja.
statement.en:
I was born in nature and grew up surrounded by it, long before I encountered anything beyond it. I spent my childhood in a house without electricity. Literally. No computer, no phone, and I watched television only occasionally, like a borrowed dream. Perhaps that is why some people find it hard to believe that I later returned to live in my family home.

Nature has always been my immediate surroundings. I experience it as an abundance of greenery, saturated with vivid, untamed colours. Flowers are everywhere—unarranged, alive, exuberant. Within them lies an entire system of forms, structures, and patterns. If you look closely enough, they begin to resemble another language. The meadow is my universe. Almost everything I remember from childhood is connected to it: flowers, grass, sun-baked afternoons… and more flowers.

Flowers? What the hell? So why is everything in black and white? Still?

For this series, I use a pre-trained neural network model for image-to-image transformation, running locally with ONNX Runtime. The model works exclusively with black-and-white images, processing information about brightness and structure and transforming the photographic material through its own interpretation of form, texture, and contrast. The resulting images are neither direct photographic records nor entirely imagined constructions. They emerge somewhere between the source photograph and the model’s internal representations.

I am interested precisely in this space of transformation, where a photographic image becomes something reconstructed rather than merely recorded—a process in which perception, memory, and machine processing intertwine.

I occasionally return to this rural environment with limited infrastructure, where my phone and digital tools are powered by solar energy. Here, technology is neither abstract nor distant. It is a practical, tangible system, shaped by its own limitations and by the conditions in which it operates. While nature is my immediate environment, technology becomes a means of observing it differently.

Working with lightweight AI models that run locally allows me to extend my photographic practice beyond the conventions of digital image processing. Rather than simply altering a photograph, I explore transformation, reconstruction, and the possibility of observing a familiar environment through a distinct visual language.

Ultimately, this work reflects my relationship with two seemingly distant worlds: the natural environment in which I grew up and the technological systems through which I now reinterpret it. I do not see technology as a replacement for nature or human perception, but as another means of expanding the boundaries of how they can be experienced.

statement.sr:
U doba brzog širenja moći veštačke inteligencije i njene izuzetne sposobnosti da nam olakša život i ubrza tehnološki napredak u svakoj oblasti (poljoprivredi, medicini, inženjerstvu…), suočavamo se i sa njenom teškom zloupotrebom. Usred sve veće zabrinutosti zbog vojne zloupotrebe naprednih AI modela, postavljamo ozbiljno pitanje sebi i drugima: da li nas AI oslobađa ili nas, zapravo, vodi ka smrti?

I mnogih drugih pitanja ima: da li će nam uskoro biti oduzeta slobodna volja? Mogu li stvari skrivene od javnosti dodatno ugroziti naše živote? Moraju li mladi vojnici i nevini civili da umiru od AI oružja, kada je smrt u ratu — u unakrsnoj vatri među ljudima — već sama po sebi besmislena?

Hajde da mislimo — nova pitanja stižu brže nego što uspevamo da ih postavimo.

Savremeno ratovanje više ne oduzima samo život — ono integriše telo u sistem. Vojnik prestaje da bude pojedinac i postaje čvor u mreži: senzor, meta, podatak. Granica između čoveka i oružja se briše, i upravo tu granicu rad vizuelno istražuje. Ali ni mi, gledaoci, nismo izvan te mreže. Dok skrolujemo kroz vesti o dronovima, AI oružju i sankcijama, i sami postajemo deo istog sistema slika — daleki, zaklonjeni ekranom, a ipak saučesnici u posmatranju.¹ Rad govori i o toj distanci: o tome kako smrt nekog drugog, posredovana algoritmom i pikselima, postaje samo još jedan sadržaj pored kojeg skrolujemo.

Za ovaj rad koristio sam necenzurisan AI model za generisanje slika, koji mi je omogućio da napravim portrete mladih muškaraca, vojnika, ranjenih žicama i čipovima, ukazujući na problem na taj način. Zatim sam generisane slike preneo na drugi uređaj putem SSTV (slow-scan television — televizija sa sporim skeniranjem) prenosa slike zvukom, imitirajući i zamišljeni prenos šifrovanih ratnih poruka i zamišljenu digitalnu komunikaciju između AI modela. Dobijene slike sam dodatno obradio ONNX Runtime modelom za povećanje rezolucije koji radi na samom uređaju, uključivši halucinirane podatke tog modela u sam rad. Slike su zatim dodatno obrađene u softveru za obradu slika.

¹ Trevor Paglen — američki konceptualni umetnik čiji rad sistematski istražuje skrivene infrastrukture nadzora, dronove, tajne vojne baze i mašinsku viziju, često spajajući umetničko snimanje sa istraživačkim metodama geografije i astronomije. Relevantni izvori:

MoMA, Trevor Paglen: It Began as a Military Experiment (2017), https://www.moma.org/collection/works/275173 — rad koji pokazuje kako je američko Ministarstvo odbrane koristilo baze ljudskih lica za razvoj tehnologije prepoznavanja lica.

Anthony Downey, „The return of the uncanny: artificial intelligence and estranged futures“, Visual Studies 40, br. 3 (2025): 462–471, https://doi.org/10.1080/1472586X.2024.2406709 — analiza Paglenove serije Adversarially Evolved Hallucinations i halucinantnog prostora AI generisanja slika u kontekstu nadzora i automatizovanog ratovanja.

Andreas Immanuel Graae i Kathrin Maurer (ur.), Drone Imaginaries: The Power of Remote Vision (Manchester University Press, 2026), pogl. 2 — Paglenovo delo u kontekstu dronovske umetnosti i „world-making“ moći dronova.
statement.en:
In an age of the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence’s power, and its extraordinary capacity to make our lives easier and accelerate our technological progress in every field (agriculture, medicine, engineering…), we are also confronted with its grave misuse. Amid growing concerns about the military misuse of advanced AI models, we pose a serious question to ourselves, and to others: does AI liberate us, or does it, in fact, lead us toward death?

And there are many other questions too: Will we soon be stripped of free will? Could things kept hidden from the public endanger our lives even further? Must young soldiers and innocent civilians die at the hands of AI weapons, when death in war — in the crossfire between human beings — is already senseless in itself?

Let us think — new questions arrive faster than we can even ask them.

Contemporary warfare no longer takes only life — it integrates the body into a system. The soldier ceases to be an individual and becomes a node in a network: a sensor, a target, a data point. The line between man and weapon dissolves, and it is precisely this line that the work visually investigates. But we, the viewers, are not outside this network either. As we scroll through news of drones, AI weapons, and sanctions, we too become part of the same system of images — distant, shielded by a screen, yet still complicit in watching.¹ The work speaks to that distance as well: to how someone else's death, mediated through algorithm and pixels, turns into just another piece of content we scroll past.

For this piece, I used an uncensored AI image-generation model, which allowed me to create portraits of young men, soldiers, wounded by wires and chips, suggesting the problem in this way. I then transmitted the generated images to another device via SSTV (slow-scan television) image transmission through sound, imitating both an imagined transmission of encrypted wartime messages and an imagined digital communication between AI models. I further processed the resulting images with an on-device ONNX Runtime upscaling model, incorporating that model's hallucinated data into the work itself. The images were then further edited in image-editing software.

¹ Trevor Paglen is an American conceptual artist whose work systematically investigates hidden infrastructures of surveillance, drones, secret military bases, and machine vision, often combining artistic image-making with research methods from geography and astronomy. Relevant sources:

MoMA, Trevor Paglen: It Began as a Military Experiment (2017), https://www.moma.org/collection/works/275173 — a work showing how the U.S. Department of Defense used databases of human faces to develop facial-recognition technology.

Anthony Downey, “The return of the uncanny: artificial intelligence and estranged futures,” Visual Studies 40, no. 3 (2025): 462–471, https://doi.org/10.1080/1472586X.2024.2406709 — an analysis of Paglen’s Adversarially Evolved Hallucinations series and the hallucinatory space of AI image generation in the context of surveillance and automated warfare.

Andreas Immanuel Graae and Kathrin Maurer (eds.), Drone Imaginaries: The Power of Remote Vision (Manchester University Press, 2026), ch. 2 — Paglen’s work in the context of drone art and the “world-making” power of drones.

statement.sr:
Rad predstavlja osvrt na stvaralaštvo Endija Vorhola kroz savremenu interpretaciju Web3 i NFT kulture.

Kreiranjem različitih varijacija, autor na sarkastičan, kritički i pomalo šaljiv način osvetljava savremenu umetnost i društvo.

Tehnika: Digitalna slika nastala na osnovu fotografskog predloška.
statement.en:
This work reflects on Andy Warhol’s artistic practice through a contemporary interpretation of Web3 and NFT culture.

By creating different variations, the artist sheds light on contemporary art and society in a sarcastic, critical, and somewhat playful way.

Medium: Digital image based on a photographic source.
